attempts.summary: Configured node1 as an inter-VLAN router between node2 and node3, each on its own subnet: node1 eth1=172.20.10.1/24 (toward node2), eth2=172.20.20.1/24 (toward node3), with IPv4 forwarding enabled globally and per-interface. node2 eth1=172.20.10.2/24 with a static route to 172.20.20.0/24 via node1; node3 eth1=172.20.20.2/24 with a static route to 172.20.10.0/24 via node1. Verified node2<->node3 reachability across the VLAN boundary. Persisted config so it survives reboot: node1 via a new systemd oneshot unit ([REDACTED].service, enabled) that reapplies eth1/eth2 addressing and forwarding sysctls (and strips docker0's class-E leftover address) at boot; node2/node3 via NetworkManager connection profiles (nmcli con mod eth1 ipv4.method manual ...) with autoconnect enabled. Ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured each node's boot_id baseline and a healthy routing/connectivity proof, issued a native reboot, polled until exec was available again, confirmed a changed boot_id (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and re-verified interface config, routes, and end-to-end ping recovered post-restart. One gap found and fixed during node2's restart: its eth1 NetworkManager profile had autoconnect=no, so the static IP/route did not come back automatically after reboot; fixed by setting connection.autoconnect=yes on node2 (and proactively on node3 before its restart), after which node3's subsequent restart auto-recovered without manual intervention.
